s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis in the axilla
salient_findings: Asymptomatic, reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
key_facts: No improvement with topical antifungal cream
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests were negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares histological features such as poorly defined vascular proliferation and presence of hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by similar histological findings, including vascular channels lined with bland endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with similar clinical and histological features, including a network of thin-walled vascular channels

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation and histological features, including the presence of hobnail-like endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border and the histological findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation with small dilated, cleftlike, irregular, thin-walled vascular channels dissecting collagen bundles are consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma. The presence of promontory signs and hemosiderin deposits also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma typically presents with more aggressive features, such as Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Spindle cell hemangioma usually has a more distinct spindle cell morphology and often presents as a solitary lesion, which does not match the description of the plaque in the case.

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Retiform hemangioendothelioma typically has a more complex, arborizing vascular pattern and often expresses HHV-8, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Hobnail hemangioma
rejected.why: Hobnail hemangioma typically has a more characteristic 'hobnail' appearance of the endothelial cells, which is not described in the histological findings of the case.
